title: Intelligent Tutor: Leveraging ChatGPT and Microsoft Copilot Studio to Deliver a Generative AI Student Support and Feedback System within Teams
extended_summary:
This paper examines how to design and evaluate an intelligent tutoring system that integrates the ChatGPT API (using GPT-4) and Microsoft Copilot Studio within Microsoft Teams. The core problem addressed is how to provide students with immediate, personalized support and feedback in online learning while also giving teachers better visibility into student progress and needs. The study is motivated by growing interest in AI-supported adaptive learning and the widespread use of Teams in the author's institutional context.

The intervention is a prototype smart tutor system embedded in the campus Microsoft Teams environment. It includes a GPT-4-based student support chatbot, automated instructional content generation and adjustment through Microsoft Copilot Studio, and a teacher dashboard for monitoring learning progress, engagement, and common difficulties. The system is intended to tailor feedback and learning resources dynamically in response to student questions, progress, and performance. The study uses a mixed-methods design, combining quantitative surveys, tests, behavioral log analysis, ANOVA and t-tests, with qualitative feedback from students.

The participants were 100 first-year undergraduate students from a Department of Communication and 4 teachers, apparently at a university in Taiwan. Students were divided into an experimental group that used the intelligent tutoring system and a control group that used traditional teaching methods supported by Teams but without the tutoring system. The intervention lasted one semester, described as approximately five months, and was implemented in a digital learning context centered on Microsoft Teams.

The paper concludes that students using the smart tutor system showed significantly higher learning motivation, classroom participation, understanding of course content, and perceptions of teacher insight than students in the comparison condition. Qualitative responses suggested that personalized learning and immediate feedback were the most valued features, though students also reported issues with system stability and interface usability. The authors argue that integrating ChatGPT and Copilot Studio into Teams can improve learning outcomes, student engagement, and teaching efficiency, while noting limitations in sample scope and generalizability.

identified_tools.name: ChatGPT
identified_tools.description: OpenAI's conversational LLM family used here via API to power a tutoring chatbot that answers student questions and provides personalized feedback.
identified_tools.use_case: Integrated with Microsoft Teams and Microsoft Copilot Studio to build an intelligent tutoring system for first-year university students, providing real-time support, tailored feedback, and adaptive learning assistance.

findings.finding_summary: Students using the smart tutor system showed significantly higher understanding of course content than the control group, based on an independent-samples t-test. Reported statistics were t=2.01, p=0.047; the paper states the experimental group outperformed traditional learning methods, but no standardized effect size was reported.
findings.measure: Understanding of course content questionnaire outcome

findings.finding_summary: The experimental group reported significantly higher learning motivation than the control group after using the smart tutor system. The reported result was t=2.34, p=0.021, with 100 students total in the study; no effect size was provided.

Students who used the smart tutor system had significantly higher classroom participation than students in the control condition. The paper reports t=2.15, p=0.034 from the group comparison, with no effect size or confidence interval reported.

Students in the smart tutor condition gave significantly higher evaluations of teachers' insight than those in the control group. The reported test statistic was t=2.48, p=0.016; no effect size was reported.
findings.measure: Evaluation of teachers' insight questionnaire score

findings.finding_summary: The conclusion states that ANOVA and independent-samples t-tests showed significant differences in unit test scores between the experimental and control groups, indicating better learning outcomes for students using the smart tutor system. However, no exact test statistic, effect size, or confidence interval for unit test scores is reported in the paper text provided.
findings.measure: Unit test scores / learning outcomes tests

findings.finding_summary: There was no statistically significant difference between groups in satisfaction with the user experience. The reported result was t=1.89, p=0.062, indicating a non-significant effect under conventional thresholds.
findings.measure: Satisfaction with user experience questionnaire score

Students who used the smart tutor system had significantly higher classroom participation than students in the control condition. The paper reports t=2.15, p=0.034 from the group comparison, but does not isolate the unique effect of Copilot Studio from the broader integrated system.

findings.finding_summary: The conclusion states that ANOVA and independent-samples t-tests showed significant differences in unit test scores between the experimental and control groups, indicating better learning outcomes for students using the smart tutor system. quality_tier_rationale: This is an empirical mixed-methods study with a comparison group and reported t-tests/ANOVA, but the paper provides limited methodological detail, no randomization evidence, and several results appear underspecified or partly descriptive. That places it below strong QED/RCT standards.
impact_tier_rationale: The study reports several statistically significant positive differences favoring the intervention, but no standardized effect sizes or confidence intervals are provided, making the magnitude of impact unclear. One measured outcome, user experience satisfaction, was not statistically significant.
